summary: PDF pages 1-2 bridge adjacent sections: motivates mean-field aggregation as a tractable approximation for large homogeneous MARL populations; then sets up stochastic games, Nash-Q learning, local neighborhoods, and the homogeneous interaction assumptions.

PDF pages 3-4 bridge adjacent sections: derives the agent-versus-mean-action approximation and the MF-Q and MF-AC update rules; then describes practical mean-action estimation and states convergence under strong visitation and stage-game assumptions. Literal retrieval anchors include Assumption 1, Assumption 2, Assumption 3.

PDF pages 5-7 bridge adjacent sections: relates mean-field MARL to graphical games, mean-field games, and scalable multi-agent learning; then evaluates Gaussian Squeeze, Ising, and battle domains at the population sizes and protocols reported by the authors. Literal retrieval anchors include Lemma 2, Proposition 1, Theorem 1.

PDF pages 8-10 bridge adjacent sections: summarizes scalability gains while leaving mean-sufficiency and cross-population generalization unproved; then lists the mean-field, stochastic-game, and MARL sources used by the paper. Literal retrieval anchors include Assumption 2.
